headline: Conserved and cis-regulatory elements mapped across salamander and butterfly genomes
label: Regulatory Element Discovery Across Genomes
summary: Chromosome-scale assemblies of large and non-model genomes now enable sequence-based identification of conserved and regulatory elements.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the identification of functional genomic elements from sequence and cross-species comparison, with high-quality assemblies as the substrate. The 32 Gb axolotl haplotype assembly, combined with multi-genome alignment, identifies more than 523,000 conserved non-coding elements. A re-analysis of Heliconius wing ATAC-seq and histone ChIP data builds a cis-regulatory atlas and a CNN enhancer predictor with AUROC 0.909. The degu chromosome-level assembly adds contiguity, gene annotation, and a reproducible pipeline. scEvoSel supplies a different axis, projecting population selection signals (DCMS scores) onto single-cell atlases to locate selection-relevant cell types in pig and chicken tissues. What is new here is the extension of sequence-based element prediction to non-model genomes, together with the coupling of selection statistics to cell-type context. None of these items models regulatory interactions directly.
